reset_presence_waveform.step_1_master_pull_LOW: Master pulls DQ LOW for ≥ 480 µs (Reset Pulse, tRSTL).
reset_presence_waveform.step_2_master_release: Master releases DQ; line begins rising toward VDD via Rp.
reset_presence_waveform.step_3_slave_wait_tPDH: After 15-60 µs (tPDH), at least one slave drives DQ LOW.
reset_presence_waveform.step_4_slave_presence_pulse: Slave holds DQ LOW for 60-240 µs (tPDL); multiple slaves' Presence Pulses may overlap into a single observable pulse.
reset_presence_waveform.step_5_slave_release: Slave(s) release DQ; line returns to HIGH via Rp; master can sample HIGH and proceed to ROM command phase.

write_1_time_slot_waveform.step_1_master_pull_LOW: Master pulls DQ LOW for 1-15 µs (typically ~10 µs).
write_1_time_slot_waveform.step_2_master_release: Master releases DQ; line rises via Rp.
write_1_time_slot_waveform.step_3_slot_idle: Line stays HIGH for remainder of 60-120 µs slot.
write_1_time_slot_waveform.step_4_recovery: Minimum 1 µs recovery before next slot.

write_0_time_slot_waveform.step_1_master_pull_LOW: Master pulls DQ LOW for ≥ 60 µs (typically 60 µs; full slot).
write_0_time_slot_waveform.step_2_master_release: Master releases DQ at end of slot; line rises via Rp.
write_0_time_slot_waveform.step_3_recovery: Minimum 1 µs recovery before next slot.

read_time_slot_waveform.step_1_master_pull_LOW: Master pulls DQ LOW for 1-15 µs to initiate Read slot.
read_time_slot_waveform.step_3_slave_response: Slave either drives DQ LOW (for bit = 0) or releases (for bit = 1) within the same slot.
read_time_slot_waveform.step_4_master_sample: Master samples DQ ~15 µs after slot start (tMSR); a HIGH sample = 1, a LOW sample = 0.
read_time_slot_waveform.step_5_slave_release: Slave releases DQ before end of slot; recovery ≥ 1 µs.

master_sample_time_window.notes: Spec calls for sample time between 1 µs and 15 µs after start of read time slot. Optimum is 15 µs (allows full cable rise time). For controlled pull-up voltage 4.5-5.5 V, slave timing variation tightens to 22-60 µs, permitting moving sample time to 21 µs (allowing 6 µs more cable charge time for heavier networks). AN148 Appendix E explicitly documents this trade-off for DS2480B.

common_waveform_pathology_examples.name: Excessive weight + resistor-only pull-up
common_waveform_pathology_examples.effect: Slow rise time during recovery — DQ may not reach valid HIGH before sample; reads borderline; long Write-0 streams starve slaves of parasitic power.

common_waveform_pathology_examples.name: Reflections on stubs and star branches
common_waveform_pathology_examples.effect: Ringing and undershoot on master falling edges; secondary edges may be interpreted as bit transitions by some slaves.

common_waveform_pathology_examples.name: Uncontrolled slave fall edge
common_waveform_pathology_examples.effect: Slave-driven Presence Pulse or Read-0 falling edge is not slew-rate controlled; can cause ringing and undershoot.

common_waveform_pathology_examples.name: Dynamic pull-up false trigger
common_waveform_pathology_examples.effect: DS2480B's dynamic pull-up may fire on ringing during falling edges, producing extra current that interferes with subsequent reads.

general_timing_rule: All time-slot timings scale by ~8× between Standard and Overdrive speeds. Reset Pulse ≥ 480 µs standard / ≥ 48 µs overdrive. Minimum slot 60 µs standard / 7.5 µs overdrive. Recovery between slots ≥ 1 µs at both speeds.

voltage_levels.controlled_pullup_advantage: When pull-up voltage is controlled to 4.5-5.5 V, slave bit-time variation narrows to 22-60 µs, allowing the master to push sample time out to 21 µs and supporting more network weight.
